messages:
marta: hey folks — quick one. I'm chasing a prod error and only have request_id=req_94b7c2a3. I tried the Console Requests view and got no hits. What's the fastest way to retrieve the full logs + trace? Need both console + CLI steps. ping @kevin
kevin: console: Observability > Requests, set time window ±5m and paste the request_id into the requestId filter. If that returns nothing try using trace_id (if you have it) or expand the time window. Also make sure you're in the right org/region. :mag:
sam: CLI is usually faster for digging. two quick commands we use: 
```
# get request metadata (returns trace_id, node, env)
redwoodctl requests get --id req_94b7c2a3 --env prod --json

# then query logs by trace id (preferred)
redwoodctl logs query --trace-id TR_03f91a2b --start "2026-03-15T10:05:00Z" --end "2026-03-15T10:10:00Z"
```
sam: if you only have request_id you can try: 
```
redwoodctl logs query --query 'request_id:"req_94b7c2a3"' --start -5m --end +5m
```
leo: common gotcha: if the request was routed to Dedicated or a different region the console search defaults to hosted indexes and may not show the logs. Kibana link (internal): https://kibana.redwood.internal/app/discover#/?_a=(index:'requests-*',query:(language:kuery,query:'request_id:%20"req_94b7c2a3"')) — paste that into the browser if you have SSO.
deploy-bot: INFO: request=req_94b7c2a3 routed_to=pool:d-prod-1 trace=TR_03f91a2b node=prod-node-7
marta: I ran `redwoodctl requests get` and it returned trace_id=TR_03f91a2b but `redwoodctl logs query --trace-id TR_03f91a2b` returned no results. Any ideas? Could sampling drop traces while logs are kept elsewhere?
kevin: yes sampling can drop spans, but logs are usually indexed. Two checks: 1) make sure the time window matches the trace's timestamp (timezone issues happen). 2) confirm which index holds the logs for that pool/region. You can run: 
```
redwoodctl infra find-logs --request-id req_94b7c2a3 --region us-west --json
```
that will show S3 path or index name if logs were archived.
sam: also try searching by span tag — sometimes proxies rewrite request ids. Example: 
```
redwoodctl logs query --query 'span.tags.request_id:"req_94b7c2a3" OR request_id:"req_94b7c2a3"' --start -10m --end +10m
```
leo: If logs were rotated to cold storage (older than 7d in prod for some orgs) `infra find-logs` will point you to the s3:// path and we have a quickdownloader: `redwoodctl infra fetch-archived-logs --s3 s3://redwood-logs/prod/... --out /tmp/logs.gz`
marta: great — infra find-logs returned an S3 path. downloading now. Quick follow-up: any tips to avoid this pain in future? We keep hitting sampled-out traces for high-traffic endpoints.
kevin: two options: 1) bump trace sampling for that service (Console > Observability > Tracing > sampling) for a short window when debugging. 2) add a targeted log alert that captures a full request dump when error-rate > threshold (we have a runbook). Also consider emitting a consistent request_id header at the edge so both traces and logs share the same id. :thumbsup:
sam: +1 on the targeted snapshot alert — it creates a pinned trace + full logs and drops a permalink into the alert incident. Saves a ton of time.
marta: awesome — thanks everyone, that should get me unstuck. I'll paste the S3 link here once the download completes in case anyone wants to look. :pray:
